One of the main factors that negatively affected my learning experience was the classroom communication process. Instead of engaging directly with students to address questions or ensure understanding, the instructor frequently relied on a particular student as a translation intermediary. This practice consumed a disproportionate amount of class time and led to unnecessary distractions. As a result, lectures often lost momentum, making it difficult to stay focused and follow the material effectively.
Additionally, the instructor appeared to communicate very effectively with certain students while not extending the same level of engagement to others. This pattern was noticeable both during class sessions and in interactions outside the classroom. Such inconsistent communication raised concerns about the fairness of classroom practices and evaluation processes, and contributed to a perception of unequal treatment among students.
At times, the instructor’s manner of interaction felt unprofessional and, from my perspective, occasionally disrespectful. Overall, these issues reflected significant shortcomings in communication skills, which further hindered a productive and inclusive learning environment.
